status_summary: On 2025-11-06 US officials confirmed and the President announced that Kazakhstan would join the Abraham Accords, which he called the first accession of his second term; Kazakhstan is not an Arab state and has had relations with Israel since 1992, so the report described the step as largely symbolic. On 2025-11-18 the President hosted the Saudi Crown Prince and announced a major non-NATO ally designation; Al Jazeera reports that the two governments signed a strategic defense agreement and that the President approved future F-35 deliveries, and that the Crown Prince said Saudi Arabia wants to join the Accords but needs a clear path to a two-state solution. No Saudi or other Arab state accession was found through October 2026.

timeline.event: US officials confirmed, and the President announced, that Kazakhstan would join the Abraham Accords; a signing ceremony was to make it official.

The President hosted the Saudi Crown Prince and announced a major non-NATO ally designation (White House video page dated 2025-11-18); Al Jazeera reports a signed strategic defense agreement, approval of future F-35 deliveries, and the Crown Prince saying Saudi Arabia wants to join the Accords given a clear path to a two-state solution.

title: Bring more Arab states, including Saudi Arabia, into the Abraham Accords
uncertainties: The Kazakhstan announcement and the Saudi defense agreement rest on news reports; the White House page read for the Saudi designation is a video page with no text of the designation, and no Federal Register designation notice was read. Searches found no new Arab signatory through October 2026, but a limited search cannot exclude unreported diplomatic steps. Whether Kazakhstan's signing ceremony took place was not established. The Mandate's aim of curtailing Chinese influence in Riyadh was not examined, and the reported Al Jazeera article does not mention China. Inference: the Mandate asks the administration to encourage accessions and strengthen the Saudi partnership, which is under way; accession by Saudi Arabia is the measurable outcome and has not occurred.
